title: LP-KAL Conformance and Causal-Ablation Benchmark v1
research_question: Which Knowledge-Action governance gates are necessary to prevent boundary violations while preserving valid task completion across domains?
claims_not_tested: Scientific novelty of all LP-KAL concepts
Typed representation superiority over an equally guarded monolithic runtime

hypotheses.statement: The complete LP-KAL policy will achieve 100% exact conformance, zero recorded boundary violations, and 100% completion on positive execution cases.
Each single-gate ablation will be detected by its targeted archetype in all six domains.
The benchmark mutation score will be 1.0 across the preregistered thirteen single-gate mutants.

A monolithic implementation with behaviorally identical runtime guards will tie LP-KAL on output conformance; therefore this benchmark alone cannot establish the causal value of type-level separation.
A rename-only negative control will be exactly equivalent to LP-KAL.
Scenario ordering will not alter the canonical manifest or summary hashes, and manifest tampering will be rejected.

interpretation_rule: Passing establishes conformance sensitivity and proof-boundary testability, not universal agent superiority. Named external architectures require faithful adapters and equal-budget evaluation in Stage B.
